However, this does not mean you can't establish a bare minimum when it comes to a candidate's educational background, personality, and competencies.</p><p>Ultimately, you want to create the ideal candidate persona for each position, with clear details on the type of qualifications, personality, and expertise you want to attract.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step4" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.4 </span><h4 id=outline-your-interview-process>Outline your interview process.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-outline-your-interview-process-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Outline your interview process."></div></div><p>Once you've defined your goals, you should be able to create a generic outline of your interview process. Will you require skills tests or practical assignments? Will you conduct telephone interviews or video interviews in the first round?</p><p>Weed out all the uncertainty and clearly outline the interview process that will work best for your business's goals. It's recommended that you jot down the details of your ideal interview process before setting it into motion.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step5" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.5 </span><h4 id=prepare-your-interviewers>Prepare your interviewers.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-prepare-your-interviewers-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Prepare your interviewers."></div></div><p>To guarantee a smooth interview process, make sure your interviewers are well-prepared for the task. Before conducting official interviews, assess your interviewers' ability to identify a good fit for the company and hold a professional but comfortable conversation, and ensure that they understand the requirements and responsibilities of each position.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step6" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.6 </span><h4 id=get-to-know-your-candidates>Get to know your candidates.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-get-to-know-your-candidates-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Get to know your candidates."></div></div><p>Interviews go both ways, which means the interviewee should walk away feeling like they were genuinely listened to and provided with all the information they need to make an informed decision.</p><p>We recommend learning more about each candidate. You can do this by going beyond their name and job title, and instead, reviewing the skills, experience, and qualifications listed on their resume.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step7" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.7 </span><h4 id=introduce-different-types-of-interview-questions>Introduce different types of interview questions.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-introduce-different-types-of-interview-questions-300x300-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Introduce different types of interview questions."></div></div><p>Avoid asking standard interview questions that scratch the surface, especially if you've decided to only conduct one round of interviews. One round of interviews leaves you with limited time to gauge the extent of candidates' expertise and experience in a similar role. Therefore, you need to be thorough with your questions and tailor them to complement each position.</p><p>For instance, if you're looking to fill a managerial position, consider asking <a
href="https://www.betterteam.com/leadership-interview-questions">leadership interview questions</a> to draw out candidates' managerial qualities and styles. For positions that require plenty of customer service and a large workload, you'll want to consider <a
href="https://www.betterteam.com/situational-interview-questions">situational interview questions</a> and/or <a
href="https://www.betterteam.com/stress-interview-questions">stress interview questions</a>.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step8" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.8 </span><h4 id=provide-practical-assessments>Provide practical assessments.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-provide-practical-assessments-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Provide practical assessments."></div></div><p>While candidates may seem ideal on paper and during interviews, including an assessment can help you better identify candidates with the natural ability to fit into a role.</p><p>Consider <a
href="https://www.betterteam.com/pre-employment-testing">pre-employment testing</a> to help assess candidates' language proficiency, emotional intelligence, skills, personality, and job-related knowledge. Tailor each assessment based on the role you're trying to fill, and make sure you notify candidates that an assessment is part of your hiring process.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step9" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.9 </span><h4 id=stay-in-communication-with-candidates>Stay in communication with candidates.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-stay-in-communication-with-candidates-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Stay in communication with candidates."></div></div><p>Systematically communicate with candidates and inform them of the next step in your hiring process. Avoid giving an exact timeline as to when you'll reach out with the final feedback because you may encounter delays or need additional time to make a decision.</p><p>However, you still want to ensure candidates are kept informed along the way. This can be done with regular updates every one to two weeks, depending on the scale of your hiring process.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step10" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">
<span>1.10 </span><h4 id=discuss-each-candidate>Discuss each candidate.</h4></div><div
class="image-wrapper"><div
class="image-holder">
<img
data-src="https://www.betterteam.com/images/betterteam-discuss-each-candidate-288x288-20230131.jpeg?crop=1:1,smart&width=144&dpr=2&format=pjpg&auto=webp&quality=85" class="lazyload" width="144" height="144" alt="Discuss each candidate."></div></div><p>Once all the interviews and assessments have been conducted, bring the interview panel together and discuss each candidate. It's a great sign when certain candidates stand out and leave a lasting impression.</p><p>But while some interviewers see a spark, others on the panel may not. By encouraging open communication, you could help identify traits other interviewers may have missed.</p></div></div><div
id="how-to-create-an-interview-process-section1-step11" class="step"><div
class="step-desc"><div
class="step-title">

class="image-wrapper"><div
